frontline_communication.snippet:
I would not recommend Maxon Air. They were assigned to me by my home warranty company to replace my A/C unit.  After the warranty company approved everything and ordered the unit, they contacted me to tell me that Maxon Air had been notified that the unit was ordered and would be ready for pick-up by noon that same day; they said Maxon Air would be contacting me. Since it was 115 degrees here in Phoenix, I decided to call them to try to get a time frame. The lady that answered the phone said she had no idea what I was talking about and that, until they got the unit, they could not order the additional parts they needed, which would take several days. I asked why they couldn't get the specs from the manufacturer to get the parts sooner and she hung up on me. I guess, as a customer, you are not entitled to ask questions. I called the warranty company to file a complaint and tell them I wanted a new company. The owner of Maxon Air called me back and when I told him I switched companies, he got defensive and it turned into a very loud argument with him threatening to sue me for slander if I filed a complaint or wrote a bad review. Sorry buddy, it doesn't work like that. You cannot be rude to your customers, threaten them, and expect good reviews. I called another, more professional company, and they had someone out right away and a new unit installed the very next day. I will be giving them a great review. It was completely unnecessary to go a week (with temperatures in the 100's) without A/C. The way in which Maxon Air handled our situation was unpleasant, unprofessional, and completely unnecessary. Do not go with Maxon Air.

I have never updated a review before but I feel it is necessary. I have never been treated so badly by a company. And he never followed through with his threat to beat me up, but people who act tough over the phone can never back it up in real life. But after a friend had a similar experience I looked into a lot of the good reviews and they are almost all fake. Telling friends to give good reviews just shows how bad this company is. I strongly recommend that even if you have to pay triple the price for another company...DO IT! You get what you pay for. What good is something if it only works for a year? You will save so much just by choosing a legitimate company and not one that is run out of some angry little mans garage. To prove my point notice how he thanks everyone that leaves a good review but never asks what he can do to fix the mistakes for the bad reviews...it’s cause he doesn’t care.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I had been a loyal customer of Firestone since moving to AZ in 2018. Brakes, alignments, rotations, oil changes, AC replacement; my wife and I would take our cars to Firestone and up until recently we always had good experiences. They're usually quick and affordable, however, this instance took 12 days to replace a coolant housing.

--On 04/23 I brought my car in at 5:13PM when the temp coolant housing cracked and leaked coolant, overheating the engine. Firestone let me know that they would get to it in the morning, Saturday. Service writer was Jordan. He called an hour later letting me know it would be $50 to even look at it.
--On 04/24 they called me letting me know they will order the parts and will receive them Saturday morning to complete by Saturday. Technician was Marcus. Quote was $749 for the housing and then $129 to flush the coolant fluid.
--On 04/25 they called me letting me know they received the housing, but was missing a part. They'll order from Kia Monday, receive Tuesday to complete the job.
--On 04/28/26 they called letting me know they were still waiting on a part, it'll be in tomorrow.
--On 04/29/26 I called, they were still waiting on the part, should be in tomorrow.
--On 04/30/26 I called, still waiting on the part, should be in tomorrow.
--On 05/01/26 I called, they said they were still waiting on the part. I went up to Firestone to get some things in my car I needed. They again said now they were waiting on a gasket. A manager would call me in the morning.
--On 05/02/26 I went up to Firestone around 10am, spoke with Scott (store manager) who told me the engine cover was put on a workbench and "grew legs and walked away", the assumption being another tech threw it away. Scott offered 10% off the bill to cover "a day or two of a rental" and a complimentary service check should I return, stating the part would be in Monday and I could get my car back and he would call me.
--On 05/04/26 I called in the evening, service told me "looks like we are still waiting on a part"... I reiterated that Scott said it would be in and the service tech said "yes, we will get the part tomorrow, Scott said if you called to let you know you'll have your car tomorrow"
At this point, due to the mistake on Firestone's part, I don't feel like I should be responsible to eat the cost of finding other transportation.
--On 05/05/26 I received the call that my car was ready. I picked up my car at 4:40pm. The bill shows nothing about the part they thew away, but it does show having received the gasket Thursday. Reflected in the bill is simply a 10% military service discount (amounting to $106).
--On 05/05 and 05/06 I attempted to call Scott. Since picking up my car, the EPB sensor has been tripped and my parking brake, auto hold, and cruise control functions do not work.
--On 05/07 I spoke with Scott, who felt the $106 to cover the cost of a day of rental and Uber up to Firestone and complimentary LOF (Lube, Oil, Filter) service was sufficient. He offered to fix the EPB sensor but my trust is non-existent at this point. My total bill came to $1,098, after the "military discount". Which was still higher than the original quoted amount, even factoring in the tax.

Take from this experience what you will. I try to be thorough when it comes to negative reviews. I understand things happen. Having a part come in without all the components once is understandable for a single day delay, but an additional component is unlikely. The clean photo attached shows the engine cover they replaced, which is probably as big as my torso. Throwing out the cover to my engine is just negligence, causing a several day delay in returning my car to me with very little compensation (if any, based on the "discount" versus original quote). There are plenty of other places in Surprise to take your car, and unfortunately, I won't be using Firestone again.

Photos attached: coolant leak, completed job (with replaced engine cover), and new warning lights my car currently has, along with line items on the bill and the total amount.

frontline_communication.snippet:
I had an extremely negative experience with the Firestone dealership at 17038 W Bell Rd in Surprise, AZ. After my initial visit on March 7 for a vibrating noise in the engine bay, the team installed new mounts. Soon after, a new grinding noise appeared on the right side of my vehicle. Across multiple visits and $3,377.90 in charges, Firestone replaced bearings, rotors, and even an axle, yet the noise persisted. It was only after repeated follow-ups that a senior mechanic admitted the problem was a bad mount they had installed incorrectly in the first place. Their poor workmanship created dangerous driving conditions for me and my family.

On top of that, the customer service was appalling. I had to call repeatedly for updates, was not informed promptly about delays due to wrong parts, and was given my car back with the airbag warning light on—something they admitted they were aware of. The store manager even told me his personal vehicle has had the airbag maintenance light on for 5 years. That may be good enough for him and his family but I expect better. Despite promises from a regional manager to discuss refund options I received no follow up. Seriously, if you're a woman or drive an older car, go somewhere else.
My mom and I (both in older cars) went in for oil changes and I asked about a replacement catalytic converter, was quoted $1300 parts&labor OR $300 labor if I brought in my own part. I said I was prepared to spend about half that so I'll bring in my own part, but I still need an oil change and new air filter, handed over my keys, and mom and I left.
A few hours later (longer than an oil change should take, and much longer than they had my mom's car for, considering they did hers while getting me a quote), they call me to tell me that my battery died while they were working on my car (?) and that a new one would be $175. A little much, but fine, even though I hadn’t had any issues with my battery, even I could acknowledge the battery was old and probably needed it or would soon. They called me 10 minutes later to tell me it was done. Seemed a little too quick between those calls, but what do I know.
So my mom drops me off to pick up my car, I tell the lady at the front desk that I'm there to pick up, she confirms my name and then just asks cash or card. Now this is where I can admit that I should have asked for an invoice--historically they have given it to me before scanning my card--and I didn’t, I just scanned my card. THEN she handed me the invoice for my signature and another for the receipt. I asked about a charge I didn't recognize: $85 for an "intake boot." The lady at the front didn't know, the first guy she grabbed didn't know, so they grabbed the biggest reason I will never go back: Anthony.
This man had the nerve to first tell me that he had called me three times, (to approve the intake boot, to notify me about the battery, and then to let me know the car was done), and refused to believe me EVEN WHEN I pulled up my phone records to show him only 2 calls. THEN he tried to tell me "details" of this supposed conversation we had as if to "prove" we had it, and wouldn't listen when I tried to suggest he might have confused me with another customer, as I recognized none of these "details." He then tried to suggest a payment plan "if this is about the money" as if I hadn't ALREADY PAID. As if I hadn't told him earlier this morning that I was prepared to spend more than I ended up spending--which in retrospect I should not have done, because I believe it made them think that they could add extraneous charges to my bill and push fixes that weren’t yet necessary. It was at that point that I demanded my keys back, because I knew that I'd never get through to them long enough for them to even consider refunding the charge I hadn't consented to, and I was done being gaslit, condescended to, and overcharged.
Not going back.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
Never use Diamond AC & Heating. I first contacted them on April 24, 2025, because they were running what looked like an amazing promotion—only $10 for a tune-up, plus you donate canned food to charity. I thought that was such a great idea, so I set it up.

When the technician arrived, he told me there was a burnt wire and a part that needed to be replaced. He said it would cost $500, which I couldn’t afford at the time. He then tried to sell me a yearly subscription plan. When I declined, he called his boss, and then came back to me saying they could “help me out” and do the repair for $200. I was grateful, because that was the best I could manage financially. He also told me that the part he was replacing was rare and could only be purchased through an AC company, so I couldn’t go get it myself.

According to their invoice, both the part and the burnt wire were replaced. I truly believed they had done the work. But after coming back from vacation a couple months later, my AC stopped working again. I called a different company, and they showed me that the exact same wire was still burnt and had never been replaced. This new technician also told me the part was nothing special—it was a basic part that could be bought anywhere. In the end, I had to spend $500 more for the repair that Diamond AC & Heating claimed they had already done.

What makes this so frustrating is that I thought they were doing me a favor, helping me out when I was in a tough financial situation. But in reality, it feels like they just saw how much money they could get out of me. I still have their invoice that lists “wire replacement” along with photos proving the wire was never changed.

So not only did I lose the $200 I paid them, but I also had to pay another $500 to fix what should have been taken care of the first time. It’s upsetting to feel like I was taken advantage of during a time when I trusted them to do honest work.

For those reasons, I cannot recommend Diamond AC & Heating.
(I added a picture of invoice because I see this company replys to almost every negative review saying they don't have any records for the reviewer)
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Customer charged for repairs that were not actually completed, requiring second payment for same work.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Services completed between 1/5 - 1/20 2026:

No complaints on the bushings, control arms, oil change, tires etc.

I had a CV Axle removed at a Firestone in Glendale, it failed and then was replaced again for free.
I assumed (wrongly) they would have taken care of things and topped off fluids. They did not.

A week in noticed things were not running great, odd shifting and outright would not shift properly.

Turns out my transmission fluids had been bled and not replaced, they do not do transmission anything here. So I was running on dry, and had no idea because they did not tell me.

I went to All About Transmissions and they topped off my fluids and saved my bacon.

I relied too much on their professionalism, and got nearly got burned BAD.

Spent $4000 here and I could have ended up with another $3000 in repairs due to negligence.

Go somewhere else brothers and sisters, you deserve better.

Edit 3/2/26:
Update, my alternator had been (apparently) underperforming for some time and finally failed. Another $600 to have that fixed by Imperial Auto Care because, Firestone had failed to find this during their "complete care" inspection.

The output on my alternator from 14.8v was measured at 9.5v, this was CERTAINLY PREVENTABLE.

I could deal with it and bemoan my rotten luck if I hadn't just footed a huge bill from supposed professionals who I trusted to have taken care of my vehicle a month prior.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Technicians failed to communicate about work they had done (draining transmission fluid) and the implications for customer.
frontline_communication.quote: had no idea because they did not tell me

frontline_communication.snippet: They repaired an inverter water pump and an oxygen sensor on my Prius. They charged me $100 for diagnostics. They said $50 of that was for a visual inspection and $50 for running codes. When I went to pick up my car, I noticed the muffler hanging lower than it was, almost touching the ground. Three days later I was driving my car and I heard something being drug on the ground. I parked my car and it was the muffler. The end of it had broken off and somehow it had come totally unwelded as well. I looked under the car and I believe 1-2 bar like pieces are missing because there’s two barlike pieces hanging down. When I called them and asked them why they didn’t tell me these were hanging down when I brought it in or that I was missing parts. I paid $100 for diagnostics including $50 for a visual. They said they noticed these metal pieces hanging down and the muffler being low. I feel like they lied to me and didn’t accept responsibility for the problems they created on my car. They caused the problems which is why they never prod me about them. They told me I could bring it in and have them look at it. Then told me they don’t work on exhaust systems. The muffler is touching the ground and I can’t drive my car because of it. Then he told me to tow it in. It’s 20 miles from where I live in Phoenix. That would probably be a $500 tow. DON’T TAKE YOUR CAR HERE!!!!! They’re not honest and they create more problems with your car when you bring it in for repairs. They also overcharge you for parts. And charge for diagnostics and clearly don’t even do it. Plus, their website says they do free diagnostics.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Customer explicitly states technicians noticed issues (muffler hanging, metal pieces) during visual inspection but failed to communicate these findings.
frontline_communication.quote: why they didn't tell me these were hanging down when I brought it in

UPDATE: Custom Air Design did come out again once the builder agreed to foot the bill (fair, considering home is brand new) and our issue was finally addressed. The noise has been greatly reduced.

-------------------------------------------
My family and I recently bought a new build home. Custom Air Design is the contracted company with the home builder.

When we moved in, the temperature inside the house never rose above 65 degrees but only a few weeks later meant higher temps in Phoenix which is when the AC finally kicked on in our new house. We immediately knew something wasn't right. There is a vibration in the wall that builds and is unbearably loud. I've lived in many homes and have never experienced anything like this...it can be heard on the other side of the house. It's actually quieter to stand next to the unit outside rather than be in our brand new house.

We of course reached out to the builder who referred us to Custom Air Design. A tech came out and spent maybe 5-10 minutes at our house. He didn't stay and listen to the noise fully inside of the house, promptly walked outside to look at the unit and that was it.

We were told a supervisor would come out but that never happened. We instead received a phone call the following week stating that Custom Air Design will not be coming out again nor will they be addressing this issue. We even had the builder reach out and their stance is unchanged. In fact, Custom Air Design wants to point fingers at the builder and say that the unit is too close to the house...which is odd considering Custom Air Design did the install and designs the units.

Regardless, the refusal to act on a very evident problem in a home that we've only owned for a month is leading us to file a complaint with the ROC.

I will update this review as this situation unfolds.
service_quality_in_session.reasoning: Technician spent minimal time and did not thoroughly examine the customer's problem before dismissing it.
service_quality_in_session.quote: A tech came out and spent maybe 5-10 minutes at our house. He didn't stay and listen to the noise fully inside of the house

frontline_communication.snippet:
I took my 4Runner in on 1/9/24. I knew someone here at the shop and brought it all the way across the valley because I trusted that it would be done right. I had brought in all Toyota parts from the Right Toyota parts counter. However since I'm not a mechanic myself I missed the coolant and thermostat. This was for a timing belt/water pump service. Dropped the truck off the night before and expected it to be done by end of the day.
I only got a call from Dave stating they needed to keep the truck a day or two extra since their technician Matthew (who still works there) is having a "bad day".
Unlike some other customers they know I run a business and the truck I need it for work. I asked if they could put it in priority to get it done so I can pick it up. Dave said yes. I had work where I needed a ladder the next day. They never called to ask if I wanted Toyota thermostat and coolant which is where the problems started.
I got it back and it seemed better on the drive home so I thought it was good. Next day I'm checking all my fluids, I notice the coolant reservoir is empty and then I looked in the radiator, yellow. I called and asked about it, why I wasn't given the option? Why my reservoir was empty. Dave told me to bring the truck in. Matthew came and put coolant in the reservoir but he was smirking and almost laughing at the fact i was there. I should have taken that as a sign he messed up the job. Anyways a week or so later and it's getting worse. I have a scan gauge tool where I can read the coolant temps, it was winter and I was getting up over 200 degrees. Which was not normal. I went  to Tucson during this time and I stalled a couple times. I was kind of weirded out since I just had the service done. I also went to Prescott a week later and both my coolant and trans were between 200 to 230. I realized I needed to get my coolant flushed and a Toyota thermostat installed after this. I made an appointment with Right Toyota to get the coolant flushed multiple pass flush and a Toyota thermostat with the jiggle valve installed. The Toyota tech which I have on audio recording said that it looked like they had mixed several different colors of coolant and it was close to a brown color (when I called today Joe was trying to state I had rust in my engine which was never noted in the ticket so I know he's BS) due to the red and yellow and possibly green coolant mixed in. I got it back with Toyota Red and the jiggle valve in the correct location, instantly my coolant temps dropped to 186 to 190 which is where it should be. I understand the aftermarket thermostat can be used in areas with cold climates but not recommended for the SW. Joe is not an engineer so he can't tell me that the jiggle valve doesn't matter. Anyways I called and let Dave know what was going on and that I  spent $356.94 and asked if Joe would reimburse, he stated that it wouldn't happen and I should have brought it back. I didn't bring it back because the last time I brought it in they didn't really address my concern about the thermostat and coolant they used. I wish I questioned the whole job and why Matthew thought it was funny I came back.
This year in April the stalling happened again. When I was on the freeway I heard a thump sound. I thought it was my throttle body and did service on it. It ran a little better. I had a job in Payson on 06/03 and coming back when I was in fountain hills it started to stall again. I got it home and called my new mechanic which is a Land cruiser mechanic. He had me have it towed in. Asked if I've done the timing belt recently? I said yes. He told me he kept hearing noises in the cover. What he found will be in pictures and videos below. It was complete Malfeasance of a job. Matthew left a washer in the cover and it caught on the sprocket causing damage to the sprocket, crankshaft sensor, belt and left a notch in the crankshaft. $1036.63 in damage. I reached out today and Joe was in complete denial mode. If you care about your vehicle do not take it to this shop.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Technician displayed dismissive and mocking behavior toward customer returning with concerns about his work.
frontline_communication.quote: he was smirking and almost laughing at the fact i was there

Sadly not a company I will call on again.
Put in a request over internet stating I needed new gaskets on dishwasher.  Stated there was no model number on dishwasher (otherwise, i would have replaced myself). Dispatcher called and made an appt and I again stated that there was no model number. She stated that it wouldn't be a problem that they would take a look when they got here and would be able to take care of it. We talked about the fee and they would also clean the machine.
Tech showed up, showed him where the leak was coming from, he took lots of pictures and then took the seals and gaskets out and went to part store.  He then called me and stated that there was 30 different types of dishwasher and they couldn't figure out which one of thr seals matched without buying them and opening each one to compare. I asked what my options were and he said he would be back and put the seals back in, he said he would call the office and have  someone call me to discuss.
He got back to my home 15 mins later, apparently the management couldn't be bothered to call me to discuss and the tech just told me, I didn't have options. I would have to buy a new dishwasher.  I was obviously upset and told him a few times, I knew it wasn't him. I asked if I would be expected to pay even though I stated clearly that I didn't know the model number, he said yes.
He put the seals back in and found a new leak. Then left after I mentioned that wasn't there before.
I tried calling the "woman owned" owner to request a refund, and the person that answered stated that HE would get back to me between 11 and noon when HE got back in.
(not woman owned like stated on website). He never bothered to call back.
Pretty disappointed on multiple levels. Had they told me they couldn't guarantee a fit without a model number, I wouldn't have wasted thier time or mine or my money.

calls_unanswered.snippet:
I contacted this company to inspect my propane grill due to a suspected leak and to provide an estimate for my indoor fireplace. The technician advised that the issue was a faulty propane tank and recommended replacing it. After he left, I found out  he had left both propane valves open for the grill and fireplace, which I promptly turned off. Upon replacing the tank and attempting to use the grill the next day, it exploded, causing significant damage to the grill and surrounding area, and resulting in burns to my beard, hair, and legs. I am fortunate to have survived.
When I reported the incident, the company avoided my calls, claiming they were in meetings, and denied responsibility, stating there was no written record regarding the grill, despite my having written documentation from the initial inquiry. Additionally, although the estimate was supposed to be free, the technician attempted to charge me $83, which I refused. The general manager eventually informed me that, after consulting with the owner, they would not take any action. This company’s negligence and lack of accountability are deeply concerning.
calls_unanswered.reasoning: Company deflected calls after customer reported a serious incident, preventing resolution attempts.

calls_unanswered.snippet:
DO NOT TRUST - It could be the end of your life!!

April 15, 2025 had an appointment at Gene's RV and A/C Repair in Mesa AZ for an oil change and the tires rotated on my 2019 Forest River Sunseeker Class C. When I picked up the RV, I waited a good 20-30 minutes for them to pull my RV from the back of the disheveled lot of numerous RV's to the front where I could access it. I paid for the service ($300) and was given the invoice with no further instructions or suggestions.

I drove back to the RV resort in Mesa and parked the RV until April 25, when I departed and headed back east.

Within the first 75 miles or so, I noticed the RV appeared to have a thumping sound on a tire (or more). I purchased a long reach tire gauge from an Auto Zone and checked the tires. I could not figure out what was causing the thumping sound and kept stopping and checking the air pressure in the tires. I eventually got so anxious and stressed from stopping and checking the tires, that I couldn't travel anymore. Found a tire service and had them check the tires. Well, I could have fallen over with what they pointed out!

The front right (passenger) tire had lost the hubcap and 4 of the 8 lug nuts and studs had sheared off, causing the wobbling that I was experiencing. I was so close to losing that wheel and being in a major accident, with severe consequences. The tire service center stated that this was caused by the failure of the lug nuts being tightened. I advised them that I had the tires rotated and oil changed in AZ, 10 days before I left. The mechanic advised that someone DID NOT torque the wheel completely. As you can see from the photos, it is obvious that the mechanic, J***, did not finish torquing the wheel. Not only that, but I had the tire center check the torque on the other tires and they stated that they were all off about 30 pounds. WOW!

So, as the tire center was working on my RV (waited for parts that were damaged: rotor hub assembly, new bearings and races, studs and lug nuts), I called Gene's RV Repair and spoke with Michelle. Gave her the information on the issue with my wheel and requested to talk to someone about it and what the mechanic, J***, failed to perform. She stated that she would have the service manager contact me. That was on April 28. I have not received any calls back from anyone at Gene's.

I called again, twice, on May 1st, 2025, and left 2 messages; again, with no call back or response. I referred to their 30-day labor guarantee that is on the invoice.

My recommendation is to NOT TRUST Gene's RV and A/C Repair. Obviously, they have too much going on to return calls and moving numerous RV's around in their lot, to bother doing the RIGHT THING and contacting customers and resolving the issues that they caused. They obviously do not want to take responsibility for their negligence. They are an RV service repair. People who travel in their RV's are not going to be in a position or location, to bring the RV back to them for labor guarantees or warranty work within 30 days. Obviously, with the damage that was done by this negligence, I was not able to drive the RV back to Gene's RV & A/C Repair to have them perform any work.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Professional Warning Regarding Schroeder’s Plumbing (now operating as On Service)

I want to provide a fair and professional warning to anyone considering using Schroeder’s Plumbing, currently operating as On Service.

I used this company for several years, both personally and for rental properties I manage. Unfortunately, my experience ultimately revealed serious issues with workmanship, communication, and accountability.

Three years ago, they performed a sewer pipe repair at my personal residence. The contract specifically stated that the homeowner would be notified if any additional issues were found in the line. I was never notified of any concerns and was told the repair was complete and satisfactory. Because my toilets had been removed due to flooding, they were unable to turn the water back on at that time. However, they did camera the line, and I have video showing a blue plastic bag still present in the pipe.

The current failure is just beyond the original repair area. Based on photos from the initial work, the line was still covered in dirt, indicating the full line was never properly inspected as claimed. Had the issue been disclosed at the time, it could have been addressed then preventing what is now a costly and invasive repair that requires tearing up my living room three years later.

Additionally, I discontinued using this company for my rental properties due to other serious concerns, including:
•	A valve replacement that left only hot water functioning, creating a potential safety hazard.
•	Inexperienced staff openly asking others how to perform the work while on site.
•	Jobs priced for multiple workers that were never fully completed.

While the company now attributes the failure to “old pipes,” this is a common excuse and not an acceptable explanation. Older plumbing systems are routinely repaired successfully when properly evaluated and disclosed.

I have been in this industry a long time and understand that mistakes can happen. What matters is transparency, professionalism, and standing behind your work. Unfortunately, this experience fell short on all three and has cost me thousands of dollars in corrective repairs.

There are many qualified and professional plumbing companies in Phoenix/ Mesa I strongly recommend choosing another provider.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Company failed to communicate discovered issues to customer despite contractual obligation to notify.
frontline_communication.quote: I was never notified of any concerns

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
Not a terrible shop per se, but there are nuances.

1) They once claimed my car needs A/C charged. Great. We charged it. There was very little improvement but ok.
Some 4 months later I come back for an oil change. They stated my A/C needs to be recharged. I brought them THEIR receipts to show they did the job a few months prior. To which the Scott guy stated he somehow missed the record of it. Ok.
2) After yet another oil change the same Scott guy stated the side markers are out on my 2004 4runner. These are small bulbs in the headlights which are very inexpensive. $600. Six hundred dollars. I almost fell from my chair. The Scott guy claimed bumper cover removal was required. Wow. I got my car from them and the first thing I did was look that up. The repair manual explicitly stated bumper cover removal IS UNNECESSARY. I replaced my side markers in 20 minutes at a local O'Reilly's. It is bold and stupid of you to assume I won't look that up. And it is bold and stupid of you to assume I can't do basic repairs.

People please be very careful with what they are telling you and definitely get a second opinion if proposed repairs are expensive. There are no reasons to believe this is an honest shop.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Shop quoted dramatically inflated price for inexpensive repair; customer declined and purchased parts at O'Reilly's instead
billing_or_intake_errors.quote: the side markers are out on my 2004 4runner. These are small bulbs in the headlights which are very inexpensive. $600. Six hundred dollars.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet: Horrible experience and price gouging at it’s finest. Only reason they even get 1 star is because that’s the only way I could post this review. Spoke with Scott and he told me it would be $2200 to replace an alternator. When I heard this, my jaw dropped and I did some more research. When I did more research, it showed the average price to replace an alternator was anywhere from $1100-$1400. I also called the Lexus dealership who I normally take my car to, but figured they would be way more expensive than anywhere else. My sales associate there told me all in it would’ve been $1330. When I called Scott back to let him know this he said he would look it over and get back to me. He did say part of the reason it was so high is because they had to remove the radiator. This is untrue because when I continued my research, you do not have to remove the radiator. You remove the radiator fan and the core plate which loosens the radiator and allows you to easily access the alternator. Scott called me back and magically was able to get it down to$1574.33 (which was still to high). He said the $2200was just an estimate. He never told me that was just an estimate until I called him out on his price gouging 100% guarantee he would’ve charged me the $2200 if I didn’t do my research. He was upset that I called him a liar and decided to use an F bomb. I wasn’t offended, but do think it’s unprofessional. When I picked up the car this morning, I had the pleasure of speaking with his associate, Mike, who I asked why they told me that the radiator needed to be removed and he said that’s what the Guideline stated. But then they realized they didn’t need to remove it. Apparently they’re inexperienced working on Lexuses. They’re gonna continue to get their repeat customers and maybe they’re bread and butter is just oil changes. For a 6 hour job they charged me $155 an hour for labor. They charged me $515.56 for a refurbished alternator. Needless to say, I will never do business with this shop again and I strongly advise others to stay away.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Initial quote of $2200 was severely inflated and only disclosed as non-binding after customer researched fair market value

See update to original post at the button (was 4 star now a 3 star)

Original post: Everything went well with two minor items that could use a little improvement in order to receive a 5 star.

1. I called to check availability and pricing first thing in the morning and waited until afternoon for a call back before driving to the store to receive this information. This didn’t effect me too much as I wanted to review how their parking lot was laid oou since the vehicle I was having tires put on was a 45’ 5th wheel and It’s takes a lot of room to maneuver. We made a plan while I was there.

2. Once I arrived with my 5th wheel, the spotter that was guiding me back to the stall where they would complete the work didn’t recognize the height of my 5th wheel and backed me into the building causing minor damage to my rear mounted ladder. I take some responsibility for this on myself for not talking directly to the spotter before we started the backing process, however I did discuss with the manager when getting my quote that I would need a spotter and expressed concern then of the height.

Everything else was outstanding so in spite of these two unfortunate issues, I will still be using this company for future tire transactions and would recommend them to prospective customers. Only advice would be if you are taking something oversized to plan ahead and ensure good understanding with a spotter should you need one.

Thank you

Updated post additions:

Big “O” Tire sent a message asking me if I was happy with my service so I clicked yes and submitted the above information, after finishing the above post I went back to my messages and was going to delete the text message but thought it was a little odd how many great reviews they had but very few low or even middle of the road rating. This prompted me to see if it would have let me review if I wasn’t happy so I clicked no and was sent to oblivion and not given a chance to rate them. My point is they are skewing their results so now I have to say buyer be where, know that you are only seeing the good results here unless a customer took the time to specifically come here to fill out a rating. Happy shopping.

PS my original post is still accurate as to that transaction.

frontline_communication.snippet:

And when all of this was going on, another unit in our house that we did use, quit working. It had always been loader than our other units, but we thought it was new, and didn't worry about it. That compressor went out too.
So either Trane quality sucks now, or something else is going on.
Regardless, with these units being under warranty, I was still billed $4,400 labor from another company to replace the two compressors.

A year ago when I was doing business with them I had them replace two units at my business. They have worked fine.

Bottom line Is I did around 90K of AC business with them within that past 18 months, and they were stone cold when we asked them to help with the labor on the unit that didn't work that never got used. And we would have paid them to fix the other unit. They couldn't even help with the labor.

They said they are only responsible up to one year for labor costs.

So buyer beware. We did a lot of business with them, and they didn't care, and won't care with your issues unless they legally have to. I'm a business owner, and with all the work I gave them, I would have helped with the unit that never worked. Whether I was lying or not.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
TL;DR: I was charged $734.85 for a 10–15 minute AC repair involving a $20 part. When I asked for a detailed invoice later, and never received one for parts and labor, and to speak with the owner, I was ignored and instead lectured by the service manager, Dan. I believe I was taken advantage of. Thought you all out there should know.

Full timeline:

My AC stopped cooling, so I called Forrest Anderson, a company I’ve used for the past four years for regular service and check ups. They said a technician could come out after 5:00 PM, but that after-hours service would be time-and-a-half—$150 instead of the normal $100 service call. I was also told parts might cost slightly more. I agreed, with the understanding that we would discuss pricing once the issue was diagnosed.

The technician arrived and called me about 10 minutes later (could see him on the security cameras), saying the issue was a failed dual run capacitor and that he had the part in his truck. Save your money and go to a real shop.

booking_friction.snippet:
This contractor was assigned to our AC claim back in February. It is now May and we have experienced nothing but headaches and frustration with this company. The service claim was left unresolved (3 months later). Sharing my experience:

Our case is assigned to technician Daniel. After his initial service visit on Feb 17, we were told the AC cooling issue should be fixed. Great. A week later, we turn the AC on and the cooling issue is still not resolved.

We call again and get a 2nd service visit scheduled and confirmed for Friday Feb 27. We then receive a call back that the tech cannot make it and will need to reschedule for Sat Feb 28th. We won't be in town, but OK. We request that the tech please give us a call back with a summary report after the service since we won't be present. We never get a call back and we're left in the dark.

I have to call the contractor back to get an update. Eventually, we're told that the entire AC unit needs to be replaced. We're ready to proceed but we're told by our Home Warranty that a report was never submitted by the technician. We have to keep calling back and forth between the Home Warranty and the contractor to make sure a report is received. Weeks go by. Great.

Eventually, we get an installation service scheduled for March 31st. We then get a call back that this date will have to be rescheduled to April 13th. We are not available so this gets pushed back to April 29th. April 29th turns to May 1st. Great.

The week of May 1st, we call to confirm the service one last time. The service is confirmed. Then, the morning of May 1st, we get a message that the appt has been cancelled with no explanation. I call back several times, but it seems my number is not being picked up anymore. No explanation, no dignity, no responsibility.

I gave them a chance to explain and resolve the issue over the phone, but it seems they don't want to talk. At this point, any public response they provide is trying to save face. I have never had such a terrible experience in my life. Our AC issue is still not resolved btw, 3 months later in May, in Arizona. Great.

frontline_communication.snippet:
This company made my elderly parents sit for TWO WEEKS in the peak of the Arizona Summer without A/C just to upsell some part and they’ll do the same to you.

Note: seems like company deletes bad google reviews/ Junior is the name of the Technician/ Refer to yelp for a REAL RATING. THIER RATING IS 2.6 on Yelp and should be lower.

I’d rate 0 if it let me. My parents AC went out in the middle of august and they needed an emergency repair. The company lied to my family. They told us our Air Conditioner unit required a speciality motor and that the “motor required” was more expensive and we would have to wait longer to receive it.

(All Air Conditioning units in the state of Arizona can run off of the basic/cheaper model!!!)

They claimed our unit was incompatible with any other kind of motor. Made my 60+ year old parents sit without AC for two weeks in the middle of August in Arizona. All so they could try and upsell a specialty part that was not even needed. The technician I talked to then went on to try and explain how he was a former manager and how other companies in the industry will scam you and how he was doing me a solid by giving me this ”great deal” The motor he was asking for was $2k alone excluding installation fees.
The technician then went on to explain how I needed to pay him for the ENTIRE BILL AHEAD OF TIME (WORK INCLUDED) before he would even order the part or set foot on my property.

I went with another company who ordered the basic motor, had them do more work then Cactus Plumbing and Air offered and my bill was 1/3rd the amount that I was told I had to PAY UPFRONT BY CACTUS AIR AND COOLING.

Lying to your customers and telling them the most expensive option is the only option is deplorable and It’s sleazy business. Tried to call the technician to learn more about the system so I could look into it myself and see if he was telling the truth, he got super defensive and started rattling off all these reasons as to why I shouldn’t look into that and a bunch of excessive nonsense. Sat there and argued with me and tried to strong-arm me into buying the most expensive option when I began to doubt his honesty. Truly, Utterly, The worst company

Oh and if you try to ask the main office about anything, they refer you to the technician.

Shoutout to : OZ Heating and Cooling. Real honest people, fast, cheap, and reliable. The complete polar opposite of Cactus Plumbing and Air

We recently attempted to use Einstein HVAC to repair our broken AC, leaving us without cool air during the peak of summer. Unfortunately, the experience was nonexistent.

Unprofessionalism: Dealing with Imad, the owner, was frustrating. He displayed a lack of professionalism throughout the process. He couldn't remember his appointments; we had to call him because he couldn't call as promised and had a rude demeanor.

Organization and Communication Issues: The entire project was marred by disorganization and poor communication. We were given unclear estimates on part arrivals, and the timeline changed frequently without any explanation. Getting updates from Imad was a challenge, and the information he provided was often inaccurate. His initial assurance that the part was in stock, only to later claim they don't even make the part, was a clear demonstration of his lack of skills and expertise in HVAC repair.

Overall, I recommend against using Einstein HVAC. Their unprofessionalism, lack of organization, and questionable technical skills resulted in a frustrating and ultimately unsatisfactory experience that left us deeply disappointed and finding another company to complete his unfinished work.

calls_unanswered.snippet: I got a new Bosch AC/heater from them and have had serious problems ever since, with no resolution. The unit compressor is way too loud and it wakes me up at night. My old cheap unit never made noises in the 10 years I had it. This brand new, top of the line unit he sold is supposed to be the quietest one available, but it is the loudest unit I have ever heard and multiple independent technicians agree the compressor noise is not normal for this unit. It is difficult to get Arizona Air to respond to any warranty or service calls. Often they will take 10+ days to reply to a call or text, if at all. I never got a response when I requested to schedule winter maintenance (which is required to keep the warranty active) so I had to have it serviced by a 3rd party. He sold a Bosch unit, but none of his workers were Bosch accredited or trained, resulting in a bad install and set up. It is also very difficult to get any troubleshooting done from workers who are not even familiar with this unit, as they continually say they only know Trane units. But he has refused to send out a Bosch Technician. There were multiple problems with the installation, including driving nails through my new roof, voiding the roofing warranty and resulting in a leak with stains on my ceiling. Also failed to specify and install correct size roof jack and return duct. Roof opening is undersized for the size unit he sold. Multiple issues of poor workmanship including a dented elbow, improperly installed vibration pads, sealing tape that is already peeling off, condensate drain that separated, condensate line installed above drain pan, holes that were not sealed, fan that was wired incorrectly, thermostat set up wrong, temperature sensor is out of specifcation. It is now more than 7 months later, and I still have no resolution on most issues, the few resolved were done at my own expense hiring a certified technician from 3rd parties. He hasn’t honored the 100% satisfaction guarantee, he does not provide superior workmanship and there is no 24/7 hour hotline or same day service as claimed on their website.This is my worst experience with a cooling/heating company ever.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Don't go here unless you like to throw your money away!
I took my motorhome in to have my generator repaired. It was backfiring and hard to start. I asked Shawn if they were certified  to work on the Onin generator, and he told me, "OH yes, we work on these all the time we'll figure it out."
To make a very long story short, 2 months later, and 3 or 4 rude phone calls from Rhonda telling me that they had to order more parts and the price was going way up, or I could come get it. Every call from her ended with the ultimatum, "or come and get it." Every time I told her," I want it fixed. That's why I brought it to you." The last call from her was on Monday, she said, " your motorhome is ready for you to pick up, the price is $796. And change." I said is it fixed, she said," Well, my husband doesn't have any more time to work on it. He said it's still popping, but it starts better.
In conclusion, after almost 2 months and  $800.00, I have my motorhome back with
the generator still backfiring, running just like it did when I took it in to be fixed. Now I have to take it to someone who actually knows how to fix it!

frontline_communication.snippet:
Marco came to my house to provide a quote for the installation of a tankless water heater.  He provided me with a verbal quote of $5,500.  Since I can buy the water heater for $1,800 online I asked Marco for a breakdown of the pricing between the water heater, the labor rate and any other parts necessary to complete the job.  At that point Marco got very frustrated and could not understand why I would want to know this information and left after trying to argue with me that I did not have the right to ask such questions.  My guess is that Marco does very good work from reading the previous reviews but if you want to work with Marco don't ask him about his pricing.

To clarify for those of you who read reviews and might consider Marco for doing your job I think he could be a very good fit.  My intent in writing the few reviews I have written is to communicate what to expect when dealing with a vendor both good and bad.  When I spoke with Marco on the phone yesterday I told him exactly what I was looking for to include a breakdown of the water heater cost, parts and labor and he sounded amenable to this.  My frustration with plumbing companies is they all want to provide a "book rate" quote without the details and I already had that from two other companies.  When I know a water heater costs $1,500 and someone wants to charge $5,500 for the heater and installation I want to know the details.  When Marco arrived and quoted $5,500 and was not willing to provide the details I was clearly frustrated.  Had Marco shared with me the information he just shared on Google I would have likely asked him to do the install.  To clarify and in response to Marco's response the nearest quote I had to Marco was $300 higher and I do not have a quote for $7,500.   I'm not sure why Marco decided to just walkout while I was asking my questions but it quickly devolved into insults thrown in both directions which is never good but Marco did apologize to me via text after he left.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Marco responded with frustration and dismissed the customer's reasonable request for pricing transparency, arguing the customer had no right to ask such questions.
frontline_communication.quote: Marco got very frustrated and could not understand why I would want to know this information and left after trying to argue with me

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I wouldn’t use them again. They have several hidden exorbitant fees despite claiming the service call is free, which makes me question their integrity. I would rather work with someone who charges for the service call but is much more trustworthy.

They advertise a $0 service call, but when you attempt to book and indicate your availability for the entire week, their first response is to offer a $150 after-hours call if you’re available today. This made me suspicious right away. Then, they try to schedule you within 24 hours of the service call.

They also claim that if the diagnosis takes more than 30 minutes, there will be an additional charge. The sneaky part is that they send a message from a different number stating that cancellations or no-shows will incur a $150 fee. billing_or_intake_errors.snippet: I’ve used this company before and had a great experience, but this time was completely different. The technician charged me $150 for a part that costs around $22, which feels like price gouging. I understand paying for labor, but charging that much for a part and unnecessary work is just wrong. When he finished the job, he even asked if this was a brand-new dishwasher — which I had already mentioned when I called — and then started bringing up how my washer and dryer were old, which had nothing to do with the dishwasher. The part he removed was completely new, and I could tell his demeanor changed once he realized that. When I asked how much it would be for the day, he told me $145 — nearly $300 total for something that didn’t need to be replaced. It’s really disappointing because I trusted this company before, but now I feel like I was taken advantage of simply because I don’t know much about appliances. All he needed to do was lift the drainage pipe, but instead, he chose to overcharge me instead of being honest. I hope the company looks into this and holds their techs accountable so other customers aren’t treated the same way.

deadline_missed.snippet:
I hired Zaxis to install a block wall in my back yard back in March, and it was finally finished the first week of July. I worked mostly with Gavin, and explained from the beginning how important communication was, as I had funds and knew how I wanted the wall done. He said he understood and he’d keep me involved in everything. That didn’t happen.

Basically it took almost four months for the project to be finished, a portion of the project wasn’t done because Gavin had doubts about the neighbor’s wall footer being stable, the crew left trash (food and drink wrappers) all over my yard, the gate was made with unfinished wooden slats, and there’s a section where water pools outside of the wall where the dirt was never leveled.

I did reach out to the company to express my concerns and spoke with Steve on the phone. He said they could build up the neighbor’s wall but they couldn’t guarantee it due to the unknown footers (understandable), but that they would charge more than the original estimate (which should have included the amount from the get-go). I decided against it. He said he would personally come and level the dirt around the wall to prevent water pooling, and that we’d shake on things before I paid.

That didn’t happen. I never met Steve. They did come with the tractor and level out the back yard, but left the section in the front. When they were done leveling things they just came to the door and asked for the payment and left.

The wall looks good and seems sturdy. I’m glad it was finally done. But due to the lack of communication, level of unprofessionalism, and overall cost, I would not recommend Zaxis Contracting.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Living out of state makes me worry about my senior parents when people like the owner of this business try to take advantage of them. Less than fifteen minutes into the service call, he proudly told them that they needed a new, $10,000 unit. He also told them that they needed specific refrigerant, but they're unit was so old that it would be impossible to find. I have my Universal EPA 608 certification, and I can confidently tell you that his statement was an OUTRIGHT LIE. I am SO relieved that they decided to get a second opinion, because the next tech was competent, efficient, had a well stocked vehicle, and most importantly, he was honest. He found a leak, fixed it, and recharged their system with the "impossible to find" refrigerant that just happened to magically be in good stock in the back of his vehicle. Also, the new tech found that Karl had left everything undone on the HVAC unit when he left the call, even the power! So, my parents also had to pay the new tech to put back what Karl had left disassembled. He did all of the repairs for $675, yet Karl wanted $10k...
